title: Courses at Grunewald and Clement Tervalon
summary: What he taught, students, and Tervalon who taught him harmony in the Navy band.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Well I'm sure that was always a problem. When you were at Grunewald's, could you tell me what courses you taught? What classes? What, what, what, do you remember what classes?

Yeah. Uh, classes, uh, trumpet, I started off with trumpet, teaching trumpet. Then harmony, theory, ear-treading and sight-singing, arranging, the principles of arranging. And, uh, that was about it, because I had, I had, I had, I had, I had, I had more students than anybody at the school.
Besides your trumpet, besides your trumpet, uh, players, yeah, you must have a lot of general students. Do you remember who else was that in your, in any of your classes?

Uh, just about all of the, uh, musicians, all of the musicians who were my, around my age. Now like guys like Melvin Lasting and, uh, uh, Milton Batiste, they couldn't go there, they were too young. Right. They hadn't been into the service.
Right. I'm thinking people who were older.

Uh, Clemett Turballon, did you know him? Sure. He was there. And, uh, now that was a guy who helped me a lot in music, because we were in the Navy together, in the same band. Oh, Clemett Turballon? Yeah. And he had been playing with Joe Robichaud's big band, and he played with, he played with, oh, a couple of other bands that traveled. Then he played, he did a lot of playing, but he never studied. He just was a gifted musician. And he taught me a whole lot about harmony. And when I, and then I learned from that, and then got, I got interested in studying harmony. Then I started studying, then I went to Xavier. I went to Xavier for a year. Xavier played in the band a year in the summer.
